Bertil Braun

I build and evaluate end-to-end machine-learning systems across language-model agents, scalable training infrastructure, and reinforcement learning. I work from experiments and model training through distributed systems, rigorous evaluation, and deployment. Most of my work is open source, with several projects available to try live.

Featured research system · Distributed self-play RL

AlphaZero-Style Chess & Go Engine

An end-to-end AlphaZero-style research platform that trains and serves neural chess and Go agents entirely from self-play. Performance-critical C++ implements the games, encoding, batched CUDA inference, and MCTS; Python orchestrates replay, multi-GPU DDP training, automated evaluation, and live deployment. The run below reached superhuman strength under the project’s Stockfish 13 calibration within a deliberately constrained compute envelope.

Selected work

LLM systems · Technical report

LLM-Light — Artifact-Addressed Execution

An experiment executor that keeps complete LLM configurations self-contained while resolving them into artifact-addressed stages over a fixed training pipeline. Compatible runs converge on shared completed artifacts; unresolved work is scheduled across a configured GPU pool, and completed stages plus supported pretraining checkpoints survive relaunches.

Technical report Artifact-addressed execution Experiment reuse GPU scheduling Relaunch recovery

Research · GEM² 2025

Scalable Automated Evaluation with LLMs

A published research framework for evaluating open-ended LLM output when no reference answer exists. Multiple evaluator models perform bidirectional pairwise comparisons and aggregate them into robust Elo rankings, producing rankings that agreed strongly with judgements from 20 domain experts.

GEM² 2025 paper Synthetic preference data Pairwise Elo Direct preference optimization

Speech · Real-time systems · Technical report

Voice-Light — Full-Duplex Streaming Voice Agent

A deployed full-duplex voice agent that listens and speaks concurrently, handles interruptions and backchannels, and executes tools. The project combines synthetic data, automatic labeling, model training, causal turn-taking, and a two-GPU streaming runtime, with a measured 783 ms median response time.

Computer vision · Live demo

GybeLock — Windsurfing Video Intelligence

A deployed computer-vision system that turns difficult shore-shot windsurfing video into selectable, stabilised rider footage. Specialised YOLO detection and pose models feed multi-object tracking and camera stabilisation.

Live demo YOLO detection Pose + multi-object tracking

Graph RL · Technical report

Graph-Based Traffic Signal Control

A topology-flexible reinforcement-learning controller for heterogeneous urban traffic networks. Its graph policy scores road movements while deterministic incidence matrices construct each junction’s legal actions, allowing one parameter set to control networks with 41–84 junctions and 2–12 phases each; on an unseen 6×6 grid it beat max pressure at every tested demand level by 3.5–10.6 completion-rate percentage points.

arXiv report Graph neural networks PPO SUMO · OpenStreetMap

LLM systems · Agents & orchestration

Agentic LLM Systems

Three separate agent-system projects: Temporal-Light, a self-hosted durable workflow engine; an evidence-gated coding runtime built on it; and an independent story narrator built from five A2A agents and four MCP tool servers. Together they demonstrate durable execution, tool-grounded software work, and multi-agent service boundaries.
